sources.title: Planning enforcement
sources.verified_claim: Enfield keeps the statutory section 188 register for enforcement, stop and breach-of-condition notices; the page notes recent legal time-limit changes and does not make a parcel-specific finding.

sources.title: Planning enforcement notices
sources.verified_claim: Havering publishes issued enforcement notices and preserves appeal status; an appeal can hold a notice in abeyance, so notice existence and current effect must be matched exactly.

sources.title: Requests for the removal of an enforcement notice
sources.verified_claim: Havering distinguishes written confirmation of compliance/no effect from withdrawal from the land-charges register; exact land and notice details are required.

sources.title: Failure to comply with a notice
sources.verified_claim: Havering states a complied notice can remain a charge on land and non-compliance may lead to prosecution, injunction or default action; candidate status cannot be inferred from borough context.

sources.title: Copies of enforcement notices and register
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth keeps the statutory enforcement-notice register and allows copies to be requested; current cases may appear in its planning database but exact land matching is required.

sources.title: Enforcement Notice Compliance Certificates (ENCCs)
sources.verified_claim: An ENCC can confirm the requirements of a specific enforcement notice have been met; it is notice-specific evidence and cannot be generalized to a candidate without an exact notice match.

sources.title: Types of formal enforcement action
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth distinguishes enforcement notices, breach-of-condition notices and other formal tools; each has different triggers and legal effects.

sources.title: Planning enforcement appeals
sources.verified_claim: Persons with an interest in land may appeal an enforcement notice before it takes effect; appeal status is material to current enforceability and must be checked exactly.
